author: T. R. Hamilton
title: Mayor Bissen advances review and removal of speed tables in Haiku following community input
text:
Mayor Bissen advances review and removal of speed tables in Haiku following community input
Mayor Richard Bissen announced on Jul. 28 the implementation of the second and third phases of Maui County’s speed table review for Haʻikū roadways, following ongoing meetings with residents and site visits. The review applies only to County roads and does not affect those under State of Hawaiʻi jurisdiction.
“Over the past several months, we’ve listened to residents, met with the community and taken a close look at these concerns,” Mayor Bissen said. “Community feedback gives us valuable insight into the challenges our residents are experiencing. We appreciate everyone who has shared their perspectives, and that input is helping us improve our processes, better address community needs and prevent similar issues in the future.”
The first phase began in April when proposed traffic-calming devices were paused after resident concerns about both quantity and type of speed tables installed. During this period, officials reviewed practices, gathered feedback through meetings—including a site visit led by Bissen—and evaluated safety improvements while minimizing unintended impacts. Inspections requested by residents were temporarily suspended due to unsafe conditions involving excessive speeding and incidents directed at Department of Public Works staff; an independent consultant was contracted to conduct evaluations.
“As we continue to work through these issues together, I ask for our community’s kōkua by driving safely and treating our roadwork crews with aloha,” Bissen said. “No County employee should have to fear for their safety while serving our community. We can have different opinions, but if we want to find solutions, those conversations must be guided by civility and respect. That is how we move forward together.”
In Phase 2, four speed tables on West Kuiaha Road will be removed beginning the week of Aug. 17 due to condition or drainage concerns; one may be relocated near 1690 W. Kuiaha Road for drainage reasons as well. Additional locations will continue being evaluated for possible removal as part of the ongoing process.
Phase 3 aims to improve how future requests are handled by exploring legislation that would establish a designated review body—creating more consistent procedures with expanded opportunities for public input based on engineering standards as well as resident feedback.
A community meeting regarding Haʻikū area speed bumps is scheduled for Aug. 26 at 5:30 p.m., featuring presenters from both county public works officials and state transportation representatives.
